input.quote: 21.1 Each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed Fees actually paid in the one month preceding the event, without exception.
input.rationale: Section 21.1 caps each Party's aggregate liability at one month of Fees and does so "without exception", which is both far below the fallback 12-month basis (and below our 6-month walk-away floor) and overrides the Excluded Claims defined in 21.3, leaving indemnification, confidentiality/data-protection, gross negligence and wilful misconduct inside the cap with no super-cap. Mutuality (21.2 exclusion of indirect damages, 21.3 carve-out definition and the Customer payment carve-out) is otherwise sound, so the shortest cure is to raise the basis to twelve months' Fees and subject the cap to Excluded Claims, bringing the clause to the fallback position; we have not pursued the preferred USD 1,000,000 floor or "paid or payable" basis.

proposal.summary: Cap raised to 12 months' Fees and Excluded Claims placed outside the cap
proposal.comment: [Playbook] A one-month cap applied "without exception" sits below our walk-away line and swallows the Excluded Claims defined in 21.3. We have moved the mutual cap to twelve months' Fees and carved Excluded Claims (indemnities, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct) out of it.

ops.oldText: 21.1 Each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed Fees actually paid in the one month preceding the event, without exception.
ops.newText: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed Fees actually paid in the twelve (12) months preceding the event.

mappings.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
